name: Question 1
problem:
Consider the following relation defined on the set $A=\{-1,2,6,9\}.$ 

$$
R=\{(-1,-1),(2,2),(2,6),(6,6)\}
$$

Select the options that make the following reasoning correct:

Since 
{{field-1}}{{field-2}}, 

the relation is 
{{field-3}}.
worked_solution:
A binary relation $R,$ defined on a set $A,$ is 

- *reflexive* if $(x,x)\in R$ for all $x\in A,$

- *irreflexive* if $(x,x)\notin R$ for all $x\in A.$

If some pairs of the form $(x,x)$ belong to a relation and others do not, then the relation is neither reflexive nor irreflexive.

In our case, the relation is defined on $\{-1,2,6,9\},$ and we have

$$
(-1,-1)\in R,\,(2,2)\in R,\,(6,6)\in R,\,(9,9)\notin R.
$$

Therefore, we can conclude the following:

$\,$ Since $(9,9)\notin R$ $\text{and }(6,6)\in R,$ the relation is $\text{neither reflexive nor irreflexive}.$

EXPLANATION

A binary relation R, defined on a set A, is

  • reflexive if (x,x)∈R for all x∈A,

  • irreflexive if (x,x)∉R for all x∈A.

If some pairs of the form (x,x) belong to a relation and others do not, then the relation is neither reflexive nor irreflexive.

In our case, the relation is defined on {−1,2,6,9}, and we have

(−1,−1)∈R,(2,2)∈R,(6,6)∈R,(9,9)∉R.

Therefore, we can conclude the following:

Since (9,9)∉R and (6,6)∈R, the relation is neither reflexive nor irreflexive.
